newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan attempts crude discharge at Taoyuan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan attempts crude discharge at Taoyuan.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroluem Corp will try to discharge crude at its Taoyuan refinery on Monday after its earlier attempt last Wednesday was stalled following a broken cable, a refinery source said.
The source said that the delay in discharging crude forced CPC to defer the startup of a 100,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude unit by at least another two days.
"If the weather is good we will restart the crude unit in two days after the first tanker has discharged. If not we may restart next week after both tankers have discharged," the source said.
Originally a company official had said that repair works to the broken cable would only take one day and predicted that the refinery would begin operations on Monday.
The crude unit was shut down on September 14-15 when the refinery's crude offloading ports were closed following an oil leak.
The Taoyuan refinery in northern Taiwan has a total refining capacity of 200,000 bpd.
As a result of the unexpected shutdown, CPC had bought additional jet fuel for October delivery.
